title: Dual-Mac Validated Engine, Default, Triage, and Laya CoreML FP16 LayerNorm Fixes (Wave 3)

hosts.m4_pro: Apple M4 Pro (Mac16,8, 48 GB, macOS 26.6, Apple9, MLX 0.32.4, --allow-contended)
hosts.base_m5: Apple M5 (Mac17,2, 24 GB, macOS 27.2.1, Apple10 NAX, MLX 0.32.4, quiescent)

methodology_notes.m4_pro_contention: All Wave 3 M4 Pro runs executed with --allow-contended due to active desktop/Compositor/VM background load.
methodology_notes.base_m5_quiescence: All Wave 3 Base M5 runs executed strictly quiescent (zero quiescence warnings, dedicated foreground accelerator access).
methodology_notes.laya_prewarm_protocol: All 6 multifunction Core ML Laya buckets (s64, s128, s192, s256, s384, s512) were verified with MLComputePlan [10538, 0, 0] and pre-warmed prior to timed Tier-1 evaluation.

laya_coreml_fp16_layernorm_rca.summary: Restored explicit two-pass centered LayerNorm across Core ML Laya buckets while preventing FP16 square overflow, FP16 subnormal variance inflation, and CoreML backend fuse_layernorm_or_instancenorm rewrite; retained split-head mb.einsum (1.44x faster than mb.matmul on Base M5 RB2).
root_causes_and_fixes: tok_emb (max|xc|=1.9, var_min=0.0007): base_inv_scale 1.0 -> 4.0 (var(u) >= 0.0112 vs FP16_MIN_NORMAL=6.1e-5, u^2 <= 58).

l14..l18 residual LNs (cum_r=1/256, max|xc|=11,255.2, var_min=7.11..14.39): s_eff_floor 1/256 -> 1/128 (ln_gain=2.0, var(u) >= 4.34e-4 vs eps_u=6.1e-5; eliminates +56% variance inflation across 10 consecutive LNs that caused RB2 75/250 -> 63/250).
l19..l27 residual LNs (cum_r=1/1024, max|xc|=31,851): max_ln_gain=4.0 preserves s_eff=1/256 (u^2 <= 15,480 << 65,504).
head/scorer LNs (hl0_n1, hl0_n2, hl1_n1, hl1_n2, sc_ln; max|xc|=1038..1346): base_inv_scale 0.25 -> 0.0625 (eliminates u^2=67,379..113,232 > 65,504 FP16 INF overflow; max u^2=7,077).

coremltools pass removal after weight quantization: removed common::fuse_elementwise_to_batchnorm, common::add_fp16_cast, and common::fuse_layernorm_or_instancenorm so 0 mb.layer_norm ops remain in model.mil.

Split-head attention comparison on Base M5 RewardBench-2 (n=250): split-head mb.einsum 37.33s vs mb.matmul 53.41s (1.44x faster), achieving 75/250 (0.3000) and max_diff=0.07494 vs gpu_bf16 (beating prior 73/250, max_diff=0.07595).
